scenes.headline: How Interference Search reasons over merged states
scenes.sub: A frontier search from Bad Theory Labs, tested on Countdown puzzles.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gooseberry! Bad Theory Labs says reasoning works better as a frontier of states than as one line of thought. Here is how it works.

scenes.text: Stop writing one transcript. Hold a frontier of real states, let the environment execute every move, merge states that paths share, and advance the survivors together.
scenes.say: Stop writing one transcript. Keep a frontier of real states, merge the ones different paths reach, and move the survivors forward together.

steps.say: Every live state expands at once.
The environment executes each move, so a branch holds the state it really reached.
Branches that land on the same numbers merge, and are judged only once.
A small trained judge scores them, and the dead ends drop away.
The best few survive and move down a level together.
On the left, the model thinking in text, repeating its own attempts.
On the right, the frontier merges and finishes in three levels. That side never runs the model.

scenes.title: Why the frontier reports three steps

left.title: One line of thought
items: Restart from the top when it dies
left.say: The baseline dives down one chain and restarts when it fails: about twenty-four steps to solve all thirty.

right.title: A frontier of states
items: Three moves is the puzzle's depth
right.say: The frontier keeps sixteen states a level. Four numbers always take three moves, so it always reports three.

scenes.title: Solved, of 30 hard Countdown problems
scenes.say: The ladder: thinking in text, three. The model as a yes or no judge, four. A probe on its hidden state, fifteen. The trained judge, which never runs the model, twenty-three.

scenes.label: distinct states in a hard four-number problem, on average
scenes.note: each search was given 200 judged positions
scenes.say: And the space is small: about a hundred and fourteen states, fewer than the two hundred positions each search got.

scenes.text: Merging pays when paths collide, lifting six-number problems from 50% to 77%. At four, breadth and a good judge do it.
scenes.say: Merging pays when paths collide: at six numbers, fifty percent becomes seventy-seven. At four, breadth and a good judge do the work.

recap: A frontier of real states, not one transcript
Merge where paths meet, drop what is dead
The win is the search and a small judge
scenes.say: To recap: real states, merged where paths meet, pruned by a small judge.
